paragraphs: This chapter defines the qualification and verification requirements applicable to the equipment under test. Test conditions, configurations, acceptance criteria, instrumentation, and required observations are defined below.

Unless otherwise specified, tests shall be performed using the approved qualification configuration. Any deviation from the specified sequence or test condition shall be documented and approved in accordance with the applicable configuration-management process.

The requirements in this chapter are organized by test environment and verification objective. Values appearing in tables constitute controlled test parameters unless explicitly identified as informational.
The equipment shall be tested in the configuration identified by the applicable qualification configuration record.
Before each test, the test article shall be inspected for evidence of damage, incorrect assembly, loose hardware, or configuration anomalies.
Test instrumentation shall have sufficient accuracy and resolution to demonstrate compliance with the applicable requirement.
Unless otherwise stated, measured values shall be recorded during the applicable test exposure.
The test article shall be installed using the approved mechanical and electrical interfaces. Mounting arrangements shall reproduce the intended installation configuration to the extent practical.
All external connections required for operation shall be identified before application of the test environment.
Environmental qualification demonstrates that the equipment continues to meet specified functional and physical requirements under representative environmental conditions.
The environmental sequence may include temperature, humidity, altitude, vibration, and mechanical shock exposures.
The equipment shall be operated while exposed to the specified operating temperature range. Functional performance shall be monitored during temperature exposure.
Temperature measurements shall be taken at representative locations identified in the instrumentation configuration.
The equipment shall remain functional throughout the specified operating temperature exposure.
The test article shall be exposed to storage temperature extremes without requiring continuous operation during the exposure.
Following storage exposure, the equipment shall be returned to the operating condition and inspected for degradation.
The equipment shall be subjected to controlled humidity conditions representative of the intended service environment.
Condensation shall be controlled in accordance with the applicable environmental test procedure.
Altitude testing shall demonstrate equipment operation under the specified reduced atmospheric pressure condition.
Electrical and functional performance shall be monitored during the applicable altitude exposure.
Thermal cycling shall expose the test article to repeated transitions between defined temperature extremes.
The test sequence shall include temperature stabilization and appropriate dwell periods before transition to the next condition.
The thermal shock test evaluates equipment response to rapid transitions between temperature extremes.
The transition rate is controlled between the defined environmental conditions. Equipment functionality shall be monitored before, during, and after the applicable exposure.
The temperature transition requirement is distinct from the steady-state operating temperature requirement.
Random vibration testing shall demonstrate mechanical robustness under the specified dynamic environment.
The test article shall be mounted using the representative mounting configuration. Control accelerometers shall be positioned as defined by the test setup.
Vibration response shall be monitored for unacceptable functional degradation or physical damage.
Mechanical shock testing shall demonstrate structural integrity following application of the specified shock pulse.
The test article shall be inspected following each applicable shock exposure.
The mechanical mounting arrangement shall reproduce the interface between the equipment and its representative installation.
Mounting fasteners shall be installed in accordance with the approved assembly configuration.
No permanent deformation or loosening that compromises the equipment shall occur during qualification testing.
Physical interfaces shall remain secure throughout applicable qualification testing.
Connector assemblies shall maintain their intended engagement and shall not exhibit unacceptable displacement, damage, or loss of retention.
Where interface force requirements are applicable, the force shall be measured using calibrated equipment appropriate to the interface.
Connector retention is considered a mechanical interface property even when the connector also carries electrical signals.
The equipment shall operate from the specified nominal electrical input supply.
Input voltage shall be measured at the designated equipment interface under the applicable load condition.
Input current shall be measured at nominal input voltage and representative operating load.
Measured current shall remain within the specified limit.
The equipment output shall remain within the specified voltage range under the applicable operating condition.
Output measurements shall be made using calibrated instrumentation with appropriate resolution.
Dielectric withstand testing shall demonstrate adequate isolation between the applicable electrical circuits and accessible conductive parts.
The specified test voltage shall be applied for the required duration.
Insulation resistance shall be measured using the specified test voltage after appropriate stabilization.
The measured resistance shall meet or exceed the specified minimum.
The equipment shall demonstrate required functional operation following completion of environmental exposures.
Functional status shall be recorded at the designated inspection points.
The equipment shall operate continuously for the specified endurance period under representative operating conditions.
Functional status shall be monitored throughout the endurance test.
Any interruption shall be recorded and evaluated against the applicable acceptance criteria.
The equipment shall be subjected to controlled interruptions of the electrical supply.
Following each interruption, the equipment shall recover to the specified functional state without unacceptable degradation.
Visual inspection shall be performed before and after applicable qualification testing.
The inspection shall identify visible cracks, deformation, loose hardware, damaged interfaces, missing components, or illegible markings.
Instrumentation shall be selected based on the parameter being measured and shall have adequate range, accuracy, and resolution.
Calibration status shall be verified before test execution.
Test data shall identify the test article, configuration, applicable test condition, instrumentation, and recorded measurement.
Raw data shall be retained in accordance with the applicable document-control requirements.
A test shall be considered acceptable when all applicable specified requirements and acceptance criteria have been demonstrated.
Failures, anomalies, or deviations shall be documented and evaluated before the test is considered complete.
Retest shall not be performed solely to obtain a passing result without appropriate engineering evaluation.
Following completion of qualification testing, the equipment shall be inspected for evidence of physical degradation.
Particular attention shall be given to mounting interfaces, connectors, housings, fasteners, and visible workmanship.
The configuration of the test article and supporting test equipment shall be identified in the test record.
Changes to controlled configuration items shall be evaluated before use in qualification testing.
The qualification sequence shall be established before test execution. Individual test order may be adjusted only when the technical rationale and applicable approvals are documented.
Environmental exposures shall be performed in accordance with the approved qualification sequence.
Any departure from the approved test condition shall be recorded as a test deviation.
The deviation record shall identify the affected requirement, actual condition, technical impact, and disposition.
At completion of testing, all applicable results shall be reviewed against the requirements defined in this chapter.
Open anomalies, deviations, and unresolved discrepancies shall be identified before final qualification disposition.
